paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the day the enemies circled on the calendar became the day everything turned around. Esther 9:1 says their plan was overturned, and the Jews overpowered those who hated them. Nobody in the provinces could stand against them, and the officials helped them (Esther 9:2-3). That tells me the plans of people who want to harm God's people don't get the last word.

Now look at what the Jews did with that win. Three times the text says they "did not lay a hand on the plunder" (Esther 9:10, 15, 16), even though the king's letter allowed it (Esther 8:11). I think that's a big deal, friend. Winning is one test, and what you reach for once you've won is a whole different test. Esther 9:5 shows a heavy day, and I'm not going to joke about it, but the plunder was left alone.

Then comes the part I love. After the fighting, they rested, and they made it a day of "feasting and joy" and a holiday for "sending gifts to one another" (Esther 9:17-19). I know a little about being sure the story was over, because I lay in the back of a junk drawer sure of it myself. So when you see joy break out after a hard stretch, friend, let that joy teach you something: the people God has His hand on get a day to celebrate. And Esther's story isn't done yet.
